ref: verifier prompt § Grouping refinements ("Golden-side shard specs come from eval.sharding.auto_shard_config; no test work per scheme") + eval/sharding.py:262 (Split.PAD default)
what: Nothing the planner/implementer/verifier reads states that auto_shard_config ceil-splits with a PADDED last shard (W=11008 -> 115 cores x 3 tiles = 345 > 344), so the design wrote "shard grid must cover W exactly" and the op refused every such geometry. The cells were masked (all at fp32_dest_acc_en=False) and would have surfaced as ~50 supported_fail only after Refinement 1; I found it by probing and had to implement strided in-shard addressing in the verifier pass.
suggest: State in the implementer/verifier prompts (and the sharding reference) the shard contract the harness generates: a *_SHARDED axis value means shards may be padded on the last core (ceil split); the op must normalize over the logical extent and never read the padding. Point at TileOffset::Strided / StridedTileRange as the kernel-lib mechanism.

ref: verifier prompt § Testing Protocol table (supported_fail / xfail_wrong_mode rows) vs eval/golden_tests/conftest.py:1-45
what: test_translated.py cells whose refusal is on a shape facet NOT in TARGET (tile alignment here) always land in a loud category: no axis can express the refusal, so a ValueError shows as supported_fail and a NotImplementedError as xfail_wrong_mode. The harness conftest expects shape-derived refusals to come through an INPUT_TAGGER + SUPPORTED + typed SupportRefusal (lenient xfail), but the verifier prompt only says "never invent taggers to bucket shapes by failure mode" and the feature_spec docstring pins the expected taggers to tag_rank — the two pull in opposite directions and it took reading conftest/feature_matrix/golden_harness to decide.
suggest: Add a rule to the verifier prompt: a contract-level shape gate the kernel enforces (alignment, rank) MUST be a tagger axis in SUPPORTED raising UnsupportedAxisValue even if TARGET does not list it; and tell the /golden-tests author to include such axes in TARGET so the dashboard gap view sees them.

ref: verifier prompt § Output Summary (verifier_report.json in <results_dir>/) + eval/verify_supported.py --output
what: The prompt says commit everything and lists verifier_report.json as a deliverable, but the CLI output is 7.4 MB (9.6k invalid_skipped entries each carrying a full axes dict) and <results_dir> is under gitignored generated/. No stated committed location or size policy; I hand-trimmed a compact copy into the op dir.
suggest: Either give verify_supported a --compact flag (summary + non-bulk categories, node ids only for bulk) or state in the prompt that the committed copy lives at <op_dir>/verifier_report.json and must be compact; keep the full artifact in the results dir.
